name: Young adult novel
hint: For ages 13 and up: a lie that grows, a friend group that cracks and a choice the protagonist makes entirely alone. Each step often becomes two or three chapters.

parts.title: Before
chapters: An ordinary day
(ca 3 %) Open on a scene where the protagonist wants something and something is already wrong, with no background lecture.
What throws everything
(ca 10 %) An event they can't ignore: a new school, a secret, a broken promise.
The decision
(ca 22 %) They choose to get involved, for a reason the reader recognises from their own life.

parts.title: New rules
chapters: New people
(ca 28 %) A new friend, a rival or a group that opens up another world and makes new demands.
The first time
(ca 35 %) The first party, the first kiss or the first lie to a parent: something new that they feel everywhere and can't take back.
Belonging
(ca 42 %) What they have to do or hide to be part of it, and what that costs someone else.
The lie grows
(ca 48 %) What they're hiding gets bigger and harder to back out of. End the chapter close to discovery.

parts.title: Everything breaks
chapters: The midpoint
(ca 52 %) A victory that turns out to be false, or a truth that changes the game.
The price
(ca 60 %) Friends, family or their sense of self pay for the protagonist's choices.
Found out
(ca 70 %) The lie comes out in front of the people who matter most, and the protagonist stands alone.
Rock bottom
(ca 80 %) They see their own part in what happened. No adult arrives to save the day.

parts.title: After
chapters: The choice
(ca 88 %) They decide who they want to be, and do something hard to prove it.
The deciding moment
(ca 94 %) The protagonist resolves the conflict by their own means, not by luck or a parent.
Who they became
(ca 99 %) An ending with hope: what has changed, and what is allowed to stay unresolved.

name: Middle-grade novel
hint: For ages 9 to 12: a problem the adults can't solve, a friend with a will of their own and a subplot at home. Sixteen chapters of just under 2,000 words.

parts.title: The start
chapters: An ordinary day
(ca 3 %) Show the protagonist at home or at school, what they want and what is already wrong, with action from the first line.
Something happens
(ca 10 %) Something unexpected upsets everyday life: a discovery, some news, a new pupil. End on a question.
Why no adult
(ca 18 %) Show why the adults can't or mustn't help, so the problem becomes the protagonist's own.
The decision
(ca 25 %) They decide to do something themselves, and take the first step before the chapter ends.

parts.title: Trying
chapters: The friend
(ca 30 %) A friend or a reluctant helper joins in, with goals of their own that aren't the protagonist's.
The first attempt
(ca 36 %) The plan almost works. Give a small win and a new obstacle.
At home
(ca 42 %) The subplot: a sibling, a parent or a rival makes life harder and mirrors the main problem.
The secret
(ca 47 %) The protagonist hides something from someone who matters a lot, and it starts to cost.

parts.title: The darkest point
chapters: The midpoint
(ca 50 %) A discovery changes everything: the problem is bigger, or different from what they thought.
The falling-out
(ca 58 %) The friends quarrel, and the protagonist is partly to blame.
Everything goes wrong
(ca 68 %) The plan falls apart in front of others, the secret comes out and they stand alone.
What they already know
(ca 76 %) Alone with it, they remember something from earlier in the book that points to a way out.

parts.title: All the way
chapters: Sorry
(ca 84 %) They seek out the friend and own their part, before the deciding moment.
The new plan
(ca 90 %) A plan built on their own strength and on the friend, not on luck.
The deciding moment
(ca 95 %) The protagonist solves the problem by their own means. The adults may come in afterwards, not before.
Back again
(ca 99 %) A hopeful ending in a scene that mirrors the opening and shows what is different now.

name: Chapter book for children
hint: For ages 6 to 9: ten short chapters with a hook in each, an adventure, and a problem the child solves on their own.

chapters: At home
(ca 5 %) The protagonist, what they wish for, and something funny or strange on the very first page.
Something happens
(ca 15 %) A surprise sets everything going. End the chapter on a question the reader wants answered.
The plan
(ca 25 %) The protagonist makes up their mind and makes a plan, ideally with a friend.
Into the unknown
(ca 35 %) The adventure begins, and at first it goes better than expected.
The first obstacle
(ca 45 %) Something goes wrong. Solve it halfway and let a new problem appear.
The falling-out
(ca 55 %) The friends quarrel or the plan falls apart. End so the child simply has to know what happens.
The hard part
(ca 68 %) The problem seems too big, and there's no adult around.
Brave enough
(ca 80 %) The protagonist works out the solution alone, using something they learned earlier in the book.
The solution
(ca 90 %) The plan is carried out, with one last surprise or a laugh.
Home again
(ca 97 %) Safe, but not quite as before. Show what they've learned without saying it.
